title: SQLite and FTS projections with full rebuild
objective: A rebuildable SQLite projection indexes entities, typed reference edges, backlinks, observations, claims, tasks, aliases, and full text from canonical files, with projection metadata that triggers full rebuild on schema-version mismatch and guaranteed no cross-context rows.
business_value: WP-230 retrieval, WP-300 projection staleness behavior, and WP-400 views all query this projection; the plan's decisive acceptance scenario requires rebuild-from-canonical equivalence.
scope: Implement src/workctx/adapters/sqlite/ using the stdlib sqlite3 module: connection management scoped to one context (database file 98_state/index.sqlite3), schema DDL, and a projection metadata table recording projection schema version, source context revision inputs, and build timestamps
Projection schema versioning per ADR 0007: a version mismatch triggers a full rebuild from canonical files — never in-place migration of projection tables

Index canonical documents into: entities (id, type, uri, title, aliases), typed reference edges with direction, derived backlinks, observations with locator metadata, claims with temporal fields and supersession links, tasks with hierarchy and waiting-on fields
FTS5 full-text index over canonical text (titles, bodies, statements) with a documented tokenizer choice and ranking-ready structure

Full rebuild API: scan the canonical tree (read-only, using workctx.domain.frontmatter and the domain models for parsing/validation), rebuild all tables atomically (build into a temporary database file, then swap via os.replace), and report counts and skipped/invalid documents without failing the whole rebuild on one bad file
Read-query API surface for later packages: entity lookup by id/uri, outbound/inbound edges, FTS search returning ranked ids, task state queries — typed functions, no SQL leakage to callers
Enforce context isolation: the adapter never accepts paths outside its context root and the database never contains rows from another context (denial test with two contexts)
Document the projection design and rebuild semantics in docs/reference/projections.md
non_goals: No retrieval ranking, context packs, or budgets (WP-230 consumes your query APIs)
No transaction engine integration or incremental writes on mutation (WP-300 wires staleness and incremental updates; this wave ships full rebuild plus queries)
No filesystem write primitives, locks, or staging (WP-200 owns those; your only 98_state files are index.sqlite3 and its -wal/-shm/tmp siblings)
No CLI commands (lead wires index rebuild at integration)
No new runtime dependencies: stdlib sqlite3 only; FTS5 unavailability on a supported platform is a stop condition, not a reason to add a dependency
deliverables: SQLite adapter package with schema, rebuild, and typed query APIs plus tests
acceptance_criteria: Rebuild equivalence: rebuilding twice from the same canonical tree yields identical query results; deleting the database and rebuilding restores them (NFR-004 path)
Projection schema-version mismatch triggers full rebuild, verified by test
Backlinks are derived from outbound canonical references and match them exactly in tests
FTS returns expected documents for fixture queries; tokenizer documented
Two-context denial test: no query against context A ever returns context B rows
A malformed canonical document is reported and skipped without aborting the rebuild
Concurrent readers during a rebuild see either the old or the new projection, never a partial one (temp-build-and-swap verified)
security_constraints: Fictional fixtures only; no secrets; the projection must not leak content into logs
SQLite is never the sole copy of user knowledge (ADR 0001) — no data may exist only in the projection
stop_conditions: FTS5 unavailable on a supported platform
Any need for a filesystem write primitive beyond your own database files
Any needed change to frozen files or pyproject.toml
